day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Check-In: Flight AC lands at 12:00 PM. No morning activities scheduled. Take the Canada Line SkyTrain from YVR Airport to downtown Vancouver (approx. $4 CAD with a Compass Card) and head to Vancouver Harbour Stay to drop off luggage. If the room isn't ready, store bags at the front desk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Granville Island Public Market Food Tour: Head to Granville Island via a short bus or False Creek ferry (mini-ferry costs ~$5 CAD one way). Explore the iconic Public Market on your own — sample fresh local produce, artisan cheeses, smoked salmon bites, and baked goods from vendor stalls. This is a budget-friendly way to graze and have lunch at the same time. Allow 2–3 hours to wander the market, browse local craft stalls, and soak up the lively atmosphere along the waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll the False Creek Seawall: Walk back along the False Creek seawall toward downtown, enjoying views of the city skyline at dusk. This is a free and scenic way to wind down after a travel day. Grab dinner at a casual neighbourhood spot near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Eat before or during your flight — no breakfast scheduled on arrival day.
meals.lunch: Granville Island Public Market: Graze on affordable market bites — try a fresh salmon sample, a pastry from Terra Breads, or a crepe from one of the market vendors. Budget ~$10–15 CAD.
meals.dinner: Japadog on Robson Street or a nearby food truck: Vancouver's famous Japanese-style hot dog stand is iconic, delicious, and very budget-friendly. Expect to spend ~$8–12 CAD. Alternatively, try a pho restaurant in the West End for a warming bowl under $15 CAD.

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day is intentionally light to account for travel fatigue and potential flight delays. Pick up a reusable Compass Card at the airport for $6 CAD (includes $3 stored fare) — you'll use it throughout the trip. June in Vancouver is mild and often partly cloudy with occasional rain; pack a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Lynn Canyon Ecology Centre & Suspension Bridge Hike: Take TransLink buses (Bus 228 from Lonsdale Quay, reached via SeaBus from Waterfront Station — total transit ~$3.25 CAD each way) to Lynn Canyon Park. This is a FREE alternative to the Capilano Suspension Bridge and equally stunning. Walk across the suspension bridge over the rushing Lynn Creek, explore lush rainforest trails, and visit the free Ecology Centre to learn about the local ecosystem. On a warm June day, the swimming holes are a refreshing bonus. Allow 3–4 hours for the full experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Lonsdale Quay Market: After returning from Lynn Canyon, stop at Lonsdale Quay Market on the North Shore waterfront before taking the SeaBus back. Browse local vendors, pick up affordable snacks, and enjoy views of the Vancouver skyline from the quay. Take the scenic 12-minute SeaBus back to Waterfront Station — the crossing itself offers spectacular harbour views for no extra cost (covered by your transit fare).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Gastown & Chinatown: Walk from Waterfront Station into historic Gastown to see the famous steam clock and Victorian architecture. Then wander into Chinatown — one of Canada's oldest — to browse shops and find a budget dinner. Rest up at the hotel after a full day of hiking and transit.

meals.breakfast: Pick up a bagel or pastry from a nearby café or grab groceries from a local supermarket (Save-On-Foods or Safeway) the night before for a cheap in-room breakfast. Budget ~$5–8 CAD.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from the hotel area or Lonsdale Quay Market — grab a sandwich, fruit, and a drink for ~$10–12 CAD and eat along the North Shore waterfront.
meals.dinner: Chinatown dinner: Try New Town Bakery & Restaurant for affordable BBQ pork buns and congee, or visit one of the many authentic Chinese restaurants for a full meal under $15 CAD. Alternatively, grab takeout dumplings for ~$8–10 CAD.

day_by_day.notes: Lynn Canyon is entirely free to enter — a major budget win compared to Capilano's ~$65 CAD admission. Wear sturdy walking shoes and bring water. The SeaBus ride to North Vancouver is a great budget sightseeing experience in itself. Check Lynn Canyon trail conditions at the District of North Vancouver website before going.

day_by_day.morning: Stanley Park Seawall Cycle & Nature Exploration: Rent a bike from Spokes Bicycle Rentals near the park entrance (approx. $8–12 CAD/hour or ~$30 CAD for a half-day). Ride the iconic 10km seawall loop around Stanley Park — one of North America's largest urban parks. Along the way, stop at Siwash Rock, Third Beach, Prospect Point for panoramic views of the Lions Gate Bridge and North Shore mountains, and the totem poles at Brockton Point. Allow 3–4 hours to ride and explore at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stanley Park Nature Walk & English Bay: After returning your bike, walk through Stanley Park's interior forest trails (free) to see towering old-growth trees. Exit the park at English Bay Beach — Vancouver's most beloved urban beach — and relax on the sand. In June, the days are long and the beach is lively. Browse the shops and cafés along Denman Street for an affordable afternoon snack.
day_by_day.evening: Davie Street Village & Sunset at English Bay: Return to English Bay around sunset (which in June can be as late as 9:15 PM) for one of Vancouver's most spectacular free experiences. The beach draws crowds for the nightly sunset. Then explore the vibrant Davie Street neighbourhood for dinner options.

meals.breakfast: Café Medina or a budget alternative: If splurging slightly, Café Medina is a Vancouver institution known for waffles and lattes (~$18–22 CAD). For a budget option, grab a coffee and muffin from Tim Hortons or a local bakery near the hotel for ~$5–7 CAD.
meals.lunch: Stanley Park Teahouse area has food trucks and snack bars — grab a hot dog, wrap, or snack near the seawall for ~$8–12 CAD, or bring a packed lunch from a nearby grocery store to eat at the beach.
meals.dinner: Davie Street neighbourhood: Try a shawarma wrap from one of the many Middle Eastern spots (~$10–13 CAD), or visit Vera's Burger Shack for a classic BC burger experience under $15 CAD. Alternatively, pick up sushi from a grocery store sushi counter (T&T Supermarket) for ~$8–10 CAD.

day_by_day.notes: Bike rentals are available right at the park entrance on Georgia Street — arrive early on a sunny June day as bikes can sell out. The seawall is flat and very beginner-friendly. Bring sunscreen and a water bottle. Stanley Park is entirely free to enter; only the bike rental costs money. English Bay sunset is a must-do Vancouver experience and completely free.

day_by_day.morning: Capilano Suspension Bridge & Rainforest Walk: Take the free shuttle from Canada Place (runs regularly in summer — check Capilano's website for schedule) to the Capilano Suspension Bridge Park. Walk across the famous 137-metre suspension bridge high above the Capilano River, then explore the Cliffwalk (cantilevered walkways along granite cliffs) and Treetops Adventure (suspension bridges through old-growth forest canopy). Note: admission is ~$65 CAD — this is the one bigger splurge of the trip, but it's a world-class experience. Book online in advance to save time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Capilano River Regional Park (Free Extension): After exiting the paid attraction, walk downstream along the free Capilano River Regional Park trails to extend your nature experience at no extra cost. Then take the free shuttle back to Canada Place and explore the Coal Harbour waterfront — a beautiful, completely free area with public art, seaplanes taking off, and mountain views. Walk the Coal Harbour seawall to Waterfront Station.
day_by_day.evening: Final Evening in Vancouver — Robson Street & Farewell Dinner: Stroll Robson Street for last-minute souvenir shopping (try the BC-made goods at local shops). Head to a final budget-friendly dinner in the West End or downtown. End the night with a walk along the waterfront near the hotel to soak in the Vancouver harbour lights.

meals.breakfast: Pick up supplies from a local grocery store the night before: yogurt, fruit, and granola for an in-room breakfast to save money before the Capilano splurge. Budget ~$5–7 CAD.
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch to eat in Capilano River Regional Park after the main attraction, or grab a snack from the Capilano café (budget ~$10–15 CAD). Eating outside the paid area keeps costs down.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Ramen Danbo or a similar ramen shop in the West End: A hearty, authentic bowl of ramen for ~$14–18 CAD is a perfect Vancouver send-off. Alternatively, grab fresh sushi from Fujiya Japanese Foods on Clark Drive for an affordable, high-quality final meal (~$12–15 CAD).

day_by_day.notes: Capilano Suspension Bridge is the highest-cost activity of the trip at ~$65 CAD — check their website for any discount codes or consider visiting on a weekday to avoid crowds. The free shuttle from Canada Place makes it very accessible without transit costs. If budget is very tight, skip Capilano and instead do a second hike in Lynn Canyon or explore Pacific Spirit Regional Park (UBC area) for free. Check departure flight timing and plan accordingly — YVR is about 25–30 minutes from downtown via Canada Line SkyTrain.

Explore the iconic Public Market, sampling fresh local produce, artisan cheeses, smoked salmon, and baked goods. A perfect low-key introduction to Vancouver's food scene after a long flight.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the False Creek waterfront back toward downtown, taking in views of the city skyline. Enjoy a relaxed dinner near the hotel to recover from travel.

meals.lunch: Graze through Granville Island Public Market stalls — try Lee's Donuts, Benton Brothers cheese, and smoked salmon samples (~$15–25 CAD)
meals.dinner: The Flying Pig (Yaletown location) — hearty farm-to-table comfort food with locally sourced ingredients; mains ~$25–38 CAD

day_by_day.notes: Use the Canada Line SkyTrain from YVR to Waterfront Station for the most affordable and direct airport transfer (~$10 CAD). Granville Island is best reached by the small False Creek Ferries (~$5 each way) for a scenic intro to the city. Keep the evening light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real.

day_by_day.morning: Stanley Park Seawall Cycle & Nature Exploration: Rent a bike from a nearby rental shop (Spokes Bicycle Rentals near Stanley Park entrance, ~$10–15/hr). Ride the iconic 10km seawall around Stanley Park, one of North America's largest urban parks. Enjoy ocean views, towering Douglas firs, and the Lions Gate Bridge panorama. Allow 2–3 hours at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Stanley Park on foot — visit the famous totem poles at Brockton Point, stroll through old-growth forest trails, and relax at Second Beach. Return bikes and walk back to the hotel along Coal Harbour waterfront promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Dine at Farmer's Apprentice or a celebrated farm-to-table restaurant in South Granville. Take a short taxi or bus to South Granville for an intimate, seasonal dinner showcasing the best of BC's local farms and producers.

meals.breakfast: Café Medina (Chinatown/Downtown) — beloved Vancouver brunch spot known for Belgian waffles and Levant-inspired dishes; ~$18–28 CAD
meals.lunch: Picnic-style at Stanley Park — grab supplies from a nearby deli or the Coal Harbour waterfront food trucks (~$12–18 CAD)
meals.dinner: Farmer's Apprentice (South Granville) — creative, locally sourced tasting-style menu; budget ~$55–75 CAD per person including a glass of BC wine

day_by_day.notes: Start biking by 9:00–9:30 AM to beat midday crowds on the seawall. June weather in Vancouver is generally mild (15–20°C) but bring a light layer. Bike rentals are plentiful near the park entrance on Denman Street. Book Farmer's Apprentice in advance as it is a small, popular restaurant.

day_by_day.morning: Capilano Suspension Bridge & Rainforest Walk: Take the free shuttle from Canada Place (runs every 15 min in summer) to Capilano Suspension Bridge Park in North Vancouver. Walk across the famous 137-metre suspension bridge over the Capilano River, then explore the surrounding temperate rainforest via the Treetops Adventure and Cliffwalk. Allow 2.5–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Capilano, head a short drive/taxi to Lynn Canyon Ecology Centre & Suspension Bridge Hike: Discover the free alternative suspension bridge at Lynn Canyon, swim in the natural swimming holes (weather permitting in June), and hike through lush forest trails. The Ecology Centre offers excellent displays on the local ecosystem. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Vancouver via SeaBus from Lonsdale Quay (enjoy the scenic 12-min harbour crossing). Browse Lonsdale Quay Market briefly before heading back. Enjoy a casual dinner near the hotel waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Jam Café or hotel breakfast near Vancouver Harbour — hearty eggs and locally sourced ingredients; ~$15–22 CAD
meals.lunch: Lonsdale Quay Market food hall (North Vancouver) — fresh fish tacos, sushi, or local sandwiches; ~$14–20 CAD
meals.dinner: Yet to Be Named Noodle House or Miku Restaurant (Coal Harbour, near hotel) — Miku offers aburi (flame-seared) sushi with harbour views; ~$40–60 CAD per person

day_by_day.notes: Capilano Suspension Bridge Park admission is ~$65 CAD per adult — book online for a small discount. Lynn Canyon is completely free, making it a great budget-conscious pairing. Wear sturdy walking shoes and bring water. The free Capilano shuttle departs from the Tourism Vancouver Visitor Centre at Canada Place.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Gastown and Chinatown on foot — Vancouver's most historic neighbourhoods are walkable from the hotel. Visit the famous Steam Clock on Water Street, browse independent boutiques, and wander through Dr. Sun Yat-Sen Classical Chinese Garden in Chinatown (admission ~$14 CAD). A peaceful and culturally rich morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Granville Island for any last-minute food souvenirs — local smoked salmon, BC artisan jams, or craft beer from Granville Island Brewing (tours and tastings available, ~$12 CAD). Alternatively, visit the Kitsilano neighbourhood for a beach walk along Kits Beach with stunning views of the North Shore mountains.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner at a beloved Vancouver local restaurant before departure preparations. Choose a spot that captures the best of Vancouver's multicultural food scene.

meals.breakfast: Revolver Coffee (Gastown) paired with a pastry from a nearby bakery — Vancouver's top specialty coffee; ~$8–12 CAD
meals.lunch: Nuba (Gastown location) — fresh Lebanese-inspired dishes with locally sourced ingredients; great vegetarian options; ~$16–24 CAD
meals.dinner: Tacofino (Gastown) for casual, flavourful Pacific-inspired tacos and burritos — a Vancouver institution; ~$18–28 CAD, or splurge at Hawksworth Restaurant for a memorable final meal (~$60–80 CAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if your flight is in the evening. The Canada Line from Waterfront Station to YVR takes about 26 minutes — budget 2 hours before departure. Pick up vacuum-sealed smoked salmon at Granville Island as a perfect Vancouver food souvenir to bring home.

trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Flight AC arrives at 12:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Upon landing, collect luggage and arrange a pre-booked luxury transfer (black car service recommended) to Vancouver Harbour Stay. Check-in, freshen up, and take in the stunning harbour views from your room.
day_by_day.afternoon: Granville Island Public Market Food Tour: After settling in, head to the iconic Granville Island Public Market for an immersive guided food tour. Sample fresh Pacific salmon, artisan cheeses, house-made charcuterie, local pastries, and seasonal produce from BC's finest vendors. A perfect introduction to Vancouver's celebrated culinary scene. (Approx. 2–3 hours)
day_by_day.evening: Dine at Farmer's Apprentice or a premier farm-to-table restaurant in South Granville. Enjoy a thoughtfully curated tasting menu highlighting hyper-local, seasonal ingredients sourced directly from BC farms. Reserve in advance and request the chef's tasting experience with wine pairings for a truly premium first night.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a light meal on the plane or grab a premium coffee and pastry at the airport lounge upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Graze and sample your way through the Granville Island Public Market during the food tour — fresh oysters, smoked salmon, artisan breads, and local cheeses make for a luxurious casual lunch.
meals.dinner: Farmer's Apprentice (South Granville) — Chef's tasting menu with BC wine pairings. Alternatively, Burdock & Co for an intimate, ingredient-driven seasonal dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your luxury airport transfer and Granville Island Food Tour in advance. Make dinner reservations at Farmer's Apprentice at least 2–3 weeks ahead as seating is limited. The hotel concierge can assist with all bookings. June weather in Vancouver is generally mild (15–20°C), so a light jacket is recommended for the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Stanley Park Seawall Cycle & Nature Exploration: Start your morning with a premium bike rental (or arrange a private guided cycling experience) and ride the iconic 10km seawall around Stanley Park. Take in sweeping views of the North Shore mountains, English Bay, and the downtown skyline. Stop at Siwash Rock, Third Beach, and Prospect Point for photographs and to soak in the old-growth forest atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Capilano Suspension Bridge & Rainforest Walk: After returning from Stanley Park, arrange a private transfer to the Capilano Suspension Bridge Park in North Vancouver. Walk across the thrilling 137-metre suspension bridge over the Capilano River gorge, then explore the Cliffwalk and Treetops Adventure among towering Douglas firs. The lush rainforest canopy in June is absolutely spectacular.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the waterfront and enjoy a sunset cocktail hour at the hotel bar or a rooftop lounge overlooking the harbour. Follow with dinner at one of Vancouver's finest seafood establishments.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast at the Vancouver Harbour Stay — opt for a full à la carte spread with smoked salmon eggs Benedict, fresh-pressed BC fruit juices, and artisan coffee.
meals.lunch: Post-seawall lunch at the Stanley Park Pavilion Restaurant, or pack a premium picnic basket arranged by the hotel concierge with local cheeses, charcuterie, and sparkling wine to enjoy at Third Beach.
meals.dinner: Blue Water Cafe (Yaletown) — Vancouver's premier raw bar and seafood restaurant. Order the Unsung Heroes menu featuring underutilized, sustainable Pacific seafood, paired with a curated BC white wine selection.

day_by_day.notes: Book Capilano Suspension Bridge tickets online in advance to avoid queues. For a truly premium experience, inquire about early-access or private guided evening lantern tours at Capilano. Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring a light rain layer as the rainforest can be cool and misty even in June.

day_by_day.morning: Lynn Canyon Ecology Centre & Suspension Bridge Hike: Venture to Lynn Canyon in North Vancouver for a more secluded and pristine nature experience. Visit the Ecology Centre to learn about the temperate rainforest ecosystem, then cross the free suspension bridge and hike through lush trails past dramatic swimming holes, waterfalls, and towering cedars. The 30 Foot Pool and Twin Falls trails are particularly rewarding. This hidden gem offers a quieter, more immersive wilderness experience than its famous counterpart.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city and spend the afternoon exploring the upscale Yaletown and False Creek neighbourhoods. Browse boutique galleries, pop into premium local shops, and take a leisurely False Creek ferry ride for scenic waterfront views. Consider a private kayak or paddleboard session on False Creek arranged through the hotel for a unique on-water perspective of the city.
day_by_day.evening: Indulge in Vancouver's celebrated fine dining scene with a reservation at one of the city's top chef-driven restaurants. Enjoy a multi-course tasting experience that highlights the best of Pacific Northwest cuisine.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast or visit Nemesis Coffee in Yaletown for a world-class specialty coffee experience paired with elevated breakfast bites.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch in Lynn Canyon Park — ask the hotel to prepare a premium charcuterie and sandwich box, or stop at a North Vancouver artisan deli such as Lonsdale Quay Market on the return journey for fresh local fare.
meals.dinner: Hawksworth Restaurant (Downtown Vancouver) — one of Vancouver's most acclaimed fine dining establishments. Request the seasonal tasting menu with sommelier-selected wine pairings for a definitive luxury dining experience.

day_by_day.notes: Lynn Canyon is free to enter and far less crowded than Capilano — ideal for those seeking an authentic, peaceful nature experience. Wear sturdy trail shoes as paths can be uneven and occasionally slippery near water features. The False Creek ferry is a charming and scenic way to travel between Granville Island, Yaletown, and Science World.

day_by_day.morning: Begin your final morning with a leisurely world-class breakfast at the hotel. Afterward, take a peaceful solo stroll along the Coal Harbour seawall adjacent to the Vancouver Harbour Stay — enjoy views of float planes, superyachts, and the North Shore mountains for one last immersive Vancouver moment. Stop at a local roaster such as Revolver Coffee or 49th Parallel for a farewell specialty coffee.
day_by_day.afternoon: Dedicate the early afternoon to last-minute premium shopping in the downtown core. Visit Robson Street, Alberni Street (luxury boutiques), or the Vancouver Art Gallery gift shop for curated local artisan souvenirs, BC-made products, and fine gifts. If time permits, enjoy a final light lunch before arranging your luxury transfer to Vancouver International Airport (YVR). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for international flights.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — check out of Vancouver Harbour Stay with a memorable farewell. Your hotel concierge should arrange a seamless black car transfer to YVR. Relax in the airport's Maple Leaf Lounge before your flight home.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent final breakfast at the Vancouver Harbour Stay — smoked BC salmon platter, eggs your way, fresh fruit, and premium coffee. Alternatively, visit Café Medina nearby for their legendary Belgian waffles and lavender rose latte.
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at Ancora Waterfront Dining & Patio (Coal Harbour) — stunning harbour views with Peruvian-Japanese-inspired Pacific seafood. Perfect for a memorable send-off meal.
meals.dinner: Airport dining at YVR or onboard — consider requesting a special meal upgrade for your flight.

day_by_day.notes: Request a late check-out from Vancouver Harbour Stay if your flight departs in the late afternoon or evening — most luxury properties can accommodate this with advance notice. Confirm your airport transfer the evening prior. Vancouver's YVR airport is approximately 30–40 minutes from downtown depending on traffic. The Maple Leaf Lounge at YVR offers premium pre-flight amenities including showers, dining, and bar service.
